title: Detectable queue-pressure instrumentation and dashboard rebuild for Console latency spikes
creator: Ethan Li
description: After a capacity surge on 2026-02-25 the Console experienced sustained tail latency and partial feature degradation for some tenants. Triage found that important internal signals (per-tenant queue depth, backpressure events, and drop reasons) were either not emitted or aggregated away, dashboards lacked tenant-level tail heatmaps, and sampled traces omitted the ingress->serve boundary span for cold KV cache eviction paths. This ticket tracks instrumentation, dashboards, alerts, runbook updates, and follow-up validation to close these observability blind spots.
impact_summary: Incident caused 3 hours of elevated Console tail latency with increased error rates for medium-to-large tenants. Engineering mitigations restored service but inability to identify tenant-specific pressure during the event slowed response. No PII exposure. Business impact: degraded UX for customers on multi-tenant dashboards; estimated revenue impact low but operational toil high.
investigation_summary: Root causes: (1) No per-tenant queue depth gauge exported from the ingress worker pool; we only had global queue depth which hid tenant skews. (2) Autoscaler reacted to average CPU, not queue latency, causing slow scale-up. (3) Traces were aggressively sampled for high-throughput paths; the ingress->serve span is not always captured, so KV cache eviction hot paths lacked correlation. Observability config (sampling and aggregation) had a retention bias away from 99.9th percentile signals.
action_items: A1: Add per-tenant queue_depth_gauge to ingress workers (owner: Nora Patel) — instrument org_id labels and export via metrics pipeline. ETA 2026-03-10.
A2: Emit queue_drop_total with drop_reason label (owner: Miguel Torres) — surface OOM/backpressure/bulk-reject reasons. ETA 2026-03-12.
A3: Add ingress_to_serve span at the worker handoff (owner: Priya Desai) — include tenant correlation key and cache evict marker. ETA 2026-03-08.
A4: Rework Console dashboards: tenant-level tail-latency heatmap, per-tenant queue depth, and drop-reason breakdown (owner: Nora Patel + Design support). ETA 2026-03-18.
A5: Create alerting rule for P99.9 latency delta and sustained queue_depth > X per tenant for 2m (owner: SRE team) — link to runbook. ETA 2026-03-20.
A6: Update runbook with troubleshooting steps for ingress saturation and include playbook to roll back recent autoscaler tuning (owner: SRE) — ETA 2026-03-15.
A7: End-to-end validation: synthetic tenant traffic test to reproduce queue growth and verify metrics, dashboards, and alert fires (owner: QA) — ETA 2026-03-22.
A8: Follow-up: audit sampling config for traces and increase retention for tail samples for 24h window (owner: Observability Platform) — ETA 2026-03-12.
runbook_updates: Added 'Ingress saturation' play path with step-by-step metric checks, remediation steps, and rollback guidance. Location: confluence link above.
Documented how to interpret queue_depth_gauge and queue_drop_total and mapped them to alert severities.
dashboards_to_update: Console/Tenant Pressure Heatmap - show per-org queue depth and 99.9 latency
Console/Ingress Overview - add drop_reason panel and top-10 tenants by sustained queue growth
SRE/Autoscaler Diagnostics - include queue depth vs CPU to validate scaling policy

serve.kv.eviction - span emitted on cache eviction with eviction_reason and bytes_freed
request.end_to_end - ensure tenant correlation id is present across sampled traces

acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant queue_depth and queue_drop metrics are emitted and visible in metrics explorer.
Dashboards show tenant-level 99.9th latency heatmap and top-10 tenants by queue growth.
Alerts fire in synthetic test and runbook reproduces known mitigation steps within defined SLA.
Trace spans correlate ingress handoff to downstream eviction and are searchable for tail cases.
notes: Keep action items granular and prefer high-cardinality tags only where we can afford metric cardinality. Follow SRE guidance to avoid cardinality explosion; preferred approach is 'top-k tenant' panels rather than unlimited series.
